Report_ID: Self-reported continuous abstinence from smoking at 1 year after the index hospitalization
Title: Bupropion for Smoking Cessation in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome
Author: Planer et al.
Comment: The Results section reports rounded percentages, not explicit abstinent counts. Following the synthesis contract, event counts were converted from the reported 31% and 33% using the arm-specific completer counts implied by one loss per arm (74 and 75), yielding 23 and 25 abstinent participants; the randomized denominators of 75 and 76 were retained and losses were treated as smoking for intention-to-treat pooling. The outcome was self-reported and not biochemically validated. No RR was reported by the paper, so risk_ratio and its CI were left null.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Bupropion hydrochloride SR plus intensive nurse-led counseling') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: Smoking cessation in hospitalized patients with acute coronary syndrome
Study Environment: Two campuses of Hadassah Medical Center; intervention initiated during hospitalization with hospital- and telephone-based follow-up
Medium: Bupropion hydrochloride slow-release or identical placebo, both with intensive nurse-led hospital- and telephone-based counseling
Content length: 8 weeks of study medication; 12 months of follow-up
Topic of Content: Smoking cessation after hospitalization for acute coronary syndrome
interaction_type: In-person hospital counseling and follow-up plus telephone counseling
Participant type: Adult smokers hospitalized with acute coronary syndrome who intended to quit
Recruitment source: Patients hospitalized with acute coronary syndrome at Hadassah Medical Center
Outcome measurement: Self-reported continuous abstinence from smoking at 1 year; not objectively or biochemically validated
Outcome variable: Self-reported continuous abstinence from smoking at 1 year after the index hospitalization

Title: Bupropion for Smokers Hospitalized with Acute Cardiovascular Disease
Author: Rigotti et al.
Comment: For the review synthesis, arm totals use 124 randomized/included participants per arm (Table 1; 248 total in the Results—Subjects section), as required by the contract, with losses counted as smokers. However, Table 2 lists the placebo efficacy-analysis denominator as N=123 because the paper excluded deaths before follow-up from efficacy analyses. Thus, the reported placebo percentage (13.9%) and reported OR (1.56, 95% CI 0.79-3.06) correspond to the paper's Table 2 analysis, while the synthesis event denominator is 17/124. The paper also states that 254 were initially randomized and 6 (3 per arm) were excluded before intervention; the extracted denominator follows the supplied pre-identified effect and the 248-person analysis cohort. No RR was entered because the paper reports an odds ratio, not a risk ratio; the arm-level counts permit downstream RR calculation.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Sustained-release bupropion plus cognitive-behavioral smoking-cessation counseling') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
domain: Smoking cessation in hospitalized patients with acute cardiovascular disease
Topic of Content: Smoking cessation after hospitalization for acute cardiovascular disease
Participant type: Adult smokers hospitalized with acute cardiovascular disease
Recruitment source: Patients admitted with acute cardiovascular disease at five hospitals
Outcome measurement: Continuous abstinence required 7-day point-prevalence abstinence at 2 weeks, 4 weeks, 3 months, and 12 months; validated by expired-air carbon monoxide at 2 and 4 weeks and saliva cotinine at 3 and 12 months. Participants lost to follow-up were counted as smokers.

Title: Bupropion for Smoking Cessation in Patients Hospitalized With Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Trial
Author: Mark J. Eisenberg et al.
Comment: The paper reports 12-month continuous-abstinence percentages but no integer event counts verbatim in the supplied text. Under the user's anti-hallucination rule, event counts and a computed risk ratio were therefore left null rather than reverse-engineered from rounded percentages. Randomized denominators (192 bupropion; 200 placebo) were recorded as required by the synthesis plan. The Figure 2 caption separately gives 12-month patient numbers of 183 and 194, apparently excluding deaths; these were not substituted for randomized denominators. The supplied OCR renders the carbon-monoxide comparison symbol ambiguously; the Methods explicitly describe the validation threshold as 10 ppm.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Bupropion sustained-release for 9 weeks plus low-intensity counseling') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Design Type: Multicenter, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled parallel-group trial
domain: Smoking cessation after acute myocardial infarction
Study Environment: Hospital initiation with clinic and telephone follow-up
Topic of Content: Smoking cessation after acute myocardial infarction
interaction_type: Medication plus counseling versus matching placebo plus the same counseling
Participant type: Adult smokers hospitalized with enzyme-positive acute myocardial infarction
Recruitment source: Patients hospitalized with acute myocardial infarction at collaborating sites
Outcome measurement: Continuous abstinence defined as self-report of 0 cigarettes smoked/day, confirmed by expired carbon monoxide at the stated threshold, at all follow-up periods; the analysis treated withdrawals and losses to follow-up as smoking.

Title: Sustained-release bupropion for hospital-based smoking cessation: A randomized trial
Author: Joel A. Simon, Carol Duncan, Joy Huggins, Sharon Solkowitz, and Timothy P. Carmody
Comment: The continuous-abstinence event counts were not printed directly: 6/42 and 9/43 were derived from the reported 15% and 21% using the arm-specific randomized denominators stated in the Abstract/Table 1 (42 bupropion, 43 placebo), as required by the synthesis plan. These percentages correspond to 6 and 9 participants after conversion to integer counts. The paper's own analyses instead excluded one death per arm and state that N=83 (41 bupropion, 42 placebo) was used; the review denominator retains all 85 randomized participants and thereby treats deaths/losses as non-abstinent. No RR for continuous abstinence was explicitly reported, so risk_ratio and CI fields are left null.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Sustained-release bupropion plus cognitive–behavioral counselling') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Study Environment: San Francisco Veterans Affairs Medical Center inpatient hospital setting
Medium: Sustained-release oral bupropion or identical placebo plus cognitive–behavioral counselling
Content length: 7-week medication course with follow-up through 6 months
Topic of Content: Smoking cessation among hospitalized adult smokers
interaction_type: Individual in-hospital counselling plus five follow-up telephone counselling calls, with medication or placebo
Participant type: Hospitalized adult smokers, predominantly male U.S. veterans
Recruitment source: Patients hospitalized for at least 24 hours at the San Francisco Veterans Affairs Medical Center
Outcome measurement: Continuous quitters were self-reported quitters at each follow-up assessment and had biochemical or proxy validation at the 6-month follow-up; salivary cotinine was used when available and spousal/significant-other proxy otherwise.
